module: The game's unit test manager (BeamNG GmbH, Thomas Fischer, 2024). It runs test functions grouped in a table (keys starting with "test", sorted), gives each test a rich `ctx` context (assert, assertEqual, assertNear, fail, success, setDescription, garbage collector checks), measures the duration and allocated memory, and returns a summary. `runTestFiles` discovers all the `*.test.lua` files in /lua/common/ and /lua/<vm>/ and runs them (e.g. mathlib.test.lua, utils.test.lua).
usage:
-- GE console:
require('testFramework/TestManager'):runTestFiles()          -- all the *.test.lua
require('testFramework/TestManager'):runTestFiles('mathlib')  -- filter by pattern
notes: Context `ctx` passed to each test: fail(message, withTraceback?), success(message), setDescription(text), assert(cond, msg), assertEqual(actual, expected, msg), assertNear(actual, expected, tolerance=0.001, msg), resetGarbageCheckpoint(), checkGarbage(maxBytes=0, msg), allowGarbage(bytes), buildFailureMessage(kind, message). A test is defined as `function M.testXxx(ctx)` (a single parameter: ctx).
A test name ending in `_shouldFail` must fail to be considered successful.

Options of `run`: resultNamePrefix, writeXml (writes the JUnit XML if outputFile is also given), suppressLogs, captureLogs (captures Engine.getFrameLog), failOnErrorLogs, testPattern (filter on the name), context, enableJit. By default the JIT is turned off (`jit.off()`, permanently for the session) for reproducibility.

Each test runs with setfenv(func, _G), a collectgarbage("collect") then `collectgarbage("stop")`: the memory allocated during the test (garbageBytes) is measured between the start and the end, then the GC is restarted.
The example at the end of the file calls `testManager:run(tests, 'test-results.xml')`; without `options.writeXml = true`, no file is written.
The tests use engine APIs: HighPerfTimer/hptimer, os.clockhp, Engine.getFrameLog, FS:findFiles, jsonWriteFile, log.
ExtensionTest.lua expects a `runSandboxedFunction` method on this manager that does not exist there, and the local function getLuaNamespacesForVmType is not exported.

currentCtx.desc: Context of the test currently running.

run.desc: Runs the tests of the `tests` table and returns the results. Logs each test (duration, garbage bytes), a final summary, and optionally writes a JUnit XML.

outputFile.desc: Path of the JUnit XML report (used only if options.writeXml).

options.desc: {resultNamePrefix, resultNameSeparator, writeXml, suppressLogs, captureLogs, failOnErrorLogs, testPattern, context, enableJit}.

returns.desc: {testPassCount, testFailCount, testResults, totalDuration (s), totalGarbageBytes}. Each result: {name, passed, description, duration, garbageBytes, allowedGarbageBytes, expectedToFail?, errorMessage?, successMessage?, logs?}.

runTestFiles.desc: Finds all the `*.test.lua` files under /lua/common/ and /lua/<vm>/ (vm "game" -> ge folder), loads them and runs the tests of those whose path (or a test name) matches `pattern`. Aggregates the results.

pattern.desc: Lua pattern applied to the file path then to the test names; nil = run everything.

options.desc: {writeResults = boolean}: writes <file>.results.json next to each test file.

setLogDefault.desc: Sets the default log level (internal field LogDefault; not used afterwards by run).

drainFrameLogs.desc: Reads the frame log (Engine.getFrameLog, under pcall) and converts it into a list {timestamp, level, origin, message}. Used to capture the logs of a test.

logsContainErrors.desc: Indicates whether a list of logs contains an error-level entry (first character of the level = E).

returns.desc: true if there is at least one error.
